item.text:
<linkedin_post>Wikipedia’s volunteer editors rely on published sources to create and maintain articles. When AI systems use those sources, the terms of that use can affect the material available to editors and readers.

In a court filing in the OpenAI copyright litigation, the Wikimedia Foundation argues that using copyrighted works to train an AI model can qualify as fair use when the resulting model is different from its sources. It takes a different position on retrieval-augmented generation and similar techniques that retrieve content to ground chatbot answers: companies should follow the relevant publisher’s licensing requirements.

For Wikipedia, those requirements include crediting creators and sharing adaptations under the same Creative Commons license. The Foundation also asks companies scraping its projects to respect public API rate limits or use its Enterprise API.</linkedin_post>
